Biostatistics helps public health workers collect, analyse, and interpret health data so they can identify health problems, compare risks, evaluate interventions, and plan services. For example, it is used to track disease cases, study risk factors, and evaluate vaccination programmes.

The mean is the sum of all values divided by the number of values; it is useful for numerical data without extreme values. The median is the middle value in ordered data, or the average of the two middle values when there is an even number; it is useful when extreme values may distort the mean. The mode is the most frequently occurring value; it is useful for identifying the most common value or category.
